scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. We've been living together for two years, and we moved to our current apartment a year ago. The main reason we moved was because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy without roommates. That worked out well until recently when J ended up moving back in with us. From what I gather, J had some issues with her previous roommates. She didn't pay rent for two months, which caused some financial strain. The landlords were accepting cash, so it's unclear if they were aware of the situation. J then got money from her family to pay off the rent and asked my girlfriend, L, and me to let her stay with us until the end of January. However, it seems like J didn't make solid plans to move out, as she mentioned possibly staying in New York instead of moving out of state with her uncle. My girlfriend, who isn't confrontational, didn't oppose J living with us for free. But now, J has been here for about four months without a job. She sometimes helps with cooking, but that's about it. She parties a lot, comes home hungover, and our place has become a hangover den. This is affecting our home life because we can't have peace and quiet. Plus, because of the current situation (I assume this refers to the pandemic), the job J had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. Despite this, she continues to go out every other night to parties, which is irresponsible and could put us all at risk if she gets sick. I want J out, but I'm conflicted because she's my girlfriend's sister. I don't think L would be happy if I spoke to J about it, even though L also wants J out. I don't want to seem like a jerk, but things have gotten so bad that I might have to take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back, and I've been trying to get L to talk to her, but L hates confrontation. I think I might have to tell J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. So, the question is: Would it be wrong for me to kick J out? Should I do it, or is there a better way to handle this situation? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the relationship. J is L's sister, so there's a family bond there. However, J's behavior is causing significant stress and disruption in our home. She's not contributing financially, she's not looking for a job, and her partying is affecting our living situation. I also need to think about the impact on L. She doesn't want to confront her sister, which is understandable, but it's causing tension in our relationship because I'm the one dealing with the stress of having J here. I don't want to make L unhappy, but I also need to protect our home and our peace of mind. Another angle is the financial aspect. We're allowing J to live with us for free, which is generous, but she's not contributing in any meaningful way. If she can't find a job or a place of her own, it's putting a strain on our resources and our relationship. I should also consider the long-term implications. If J continues this behavior, it could lead to more problems down the line. It's better to address it now before things get worse. On the other hand, J might be going through a tough time, and we might be in a position to help her. But she needs to take responsibility for her actions and start contributing. If she can't do that, then it's fair to ask her to leave. I think the key here is communication. I should talk to L about how I'm feeling and see if we can approach J together. Maybe setting some boundaries or conditions for her staying. If that doesn't work, then it might be necessary to ask her to leave. But I'm still conflicted because it's her sister, and I don't want to cause family issues. However, our home and our relationship should come first. If J can't respect that, then it's better for her to find another place. In conclusion, while it's difficult, I think it's necessary to ask J to leave if she can't change her behavior. It's about protecting our home and our relationship with L. It's not easy, but it might be the right thing to do.
